title: Harvard’s $699 startup bootcamp integrates AI avatars for instructor feedback
summary: Harvard Business School (HBS) has launched an eight-week, $699 startup bootcamp called HBS Foundry, which uses AI avatars of instructors to provide personalized feedback during practice pitches and board meetings. The avatars, developed by startup HeyGen, were introduced after students requested a more guided experience than a simple chatbot. While some participants find the AI avatars helpful, others, including instructors like Jeff Bussgang, describe them as slightly unsettling but effective for student engagement.
key_points: HBS Foundry is an eight-week, $699 bootcamp for entrepreneurs.
AI avatars of instructors, created by HeyGen, provide feedback during practice pitches and board meetings.
The AI component was initially envisioned as a chatbot but evolved into a more guided experience based on student feedback.
Participants generally appreciate the AI avatars, though some instructors find them 'creepy' but effective.
The program includes live sessions with instructors alongside AI-driven feedback.
